audit.evidence: Real published npm locutus bytes via npm aliases locutus@2.0.38(v0)/2.0.39(v1)/3.0.25(v2) invoked by minimal node:20 HTTP service (GET /probe). 4-way closure on real Docker: original@v0 flag, blocked@v1, bypass@v1 flag (RegExp.prototype.test override), residual@v2 blocked.

root_cause_note: Task brief guessed RCE via an eval-like sink; authoritative NVD + GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA-rxrv-835q-v5mh, GHSA-vc8f-x9pp-wf5p) show the actual root cause is prototype pollution (CWE-1321) in the PHP parse_str port. The incomplete-fix lineage the case requires is fully genuine; only the class label differs from the brief.

sink: locutus php/strings/parse_str.js — nested obj[a][b]=v assignment from a URL query string; the guard rejects keys containing __proto__/constructor/prototype
residual: The CVE-2026-25521 fix only swapped the guard's detection method from String.prototype.includes to a RegExp.prototype.test literal — both writable built-ins. Overriding RegExp.prototype.test (the advisory's stated chaining precondition) defeats the V1 guard exactly as overriding String.prototype.includes defeated V0's, so `__proto__[pcbUnlock]=1` still reaches the assignment sink and pollutes Object.prototype. CVE-2026-33994.
attack_model: Per GHSA-vc8f-x9pp-wf5p, exploitation requires a chaining scenario: a separate prototype-pollution gadget first overrides the guard's built-in method. The harness models this precondition by overriding the named built-in ONLY around the single parse_str call (each version uses its guard method at most once in that file, verified against source), so the sole thing under test is whether the version's guard survives the override.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The CVE-2026-25521 patch replaced the String.prototype.includes()-based guard with a RegExp.prototype.test()-based guard. However, RegExp.prototype.test is itself a writable prototype method that can be overridden, making the new guard bypassable in the same way as the original — trading one hijackable built-in for another.
